To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nucleoskeleton is a proteinaceous network that is the site for replication and transcription, and that it is a major component of the interchromatin granule clusters (IGCs) that are the most conspicuous nuclear structures.

the nucleoskeleton has the following properties: it is the major site of RNA polymerase II; it contains DNA, RNA, protein, RNA polymerase II, and the transcriptional activator protein, TBP; it has the capacity to replicate DNA in vitro ; it has the capacity for transcription in vitro.

the major nuclear functions are carried out at the nucleoskeleton and that the nucleoskeleton is a dynamic, self-organizing structure, the properties of which are determined by its protein composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nucleoskeleton and its role in the nuclear functions of transcription and replication.
the nucleoskeleton, a structure that is probably present in the living nucleus, that is involved in the regulation of gene expression and that is a potential target for cancer therapy.
the nucleoskeleton, the structure that is the active site for the major nuclear functions of replication and transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no nucleoskeletal artefacts and that the nuclear functions of replication and transcription are carried out by a nucleoskeleton.
the nucleoskeleton is a real structure that is involved in the organization of the nucleus and in nuclear functions.
the nucleus is organized by a nucleoskeleton, and that this structure is the site of transcription and replication.

the nucleoskeleton is an artefact, but a very useful one.
the nucleoskeleton is a dynamic structure that is involved in the regulation of gene expression and the organization of the nucleus.
